title: Luciana Gimenez reveals details of her new home in São Paulo
seoTitle: Luciana Gimenez reveals details of her new home in São.
subtitle: The TV host shares her vision for the Pinheiros River and a collection by renowned artists
excerpt: Luciana Gimenez, 56, lives in a 750 sqm triplex in São Paulo's south zone. The home, renovated in 2020, features works by Di Cavalcanti, Jeff Koons, and more.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Luciana Gimenez, the TV host, settled into a 750 sqm triplex in São Paulo's south zone in 2020, during a period of personal changes. The property, which was already part of her condominium, was chosen for its open view of the Pinheiros River and the city.

Renovation and Architectural Project

The project involved architect Renan Altera, founder of Altera Arquitetura, who adapted the residence to a contemporary style, replacing the previous neoclassical decor with lighter and more functional environments. The project faced interruptions due to the pandemic, which temporarily halted factories.

Artworks and Personal Objects

  • Pieces by Di Cavalcanti, Claudio Tozzi, Jeff Koons, and Damien Hirst
  • Autographed portraits of Mick Jagger, John Lennon, and Yoko Ono
  • Objects acquired during travels and gifts received throughout her life
  • Reserved space for an artwork by Os Gêmeos, still in progress, featuring works by artist Vermelho Steam

Practical and Cozy Environments

Luciana prioritized functional furniture, such as sofas and armchairs, to create a home where “you like to sit, throw parties, and feel good.” The pastel-toned kitchen and the shoe-dedicated closet are examples of spaces designed for daily life.

“Floating House” and the View of the Pinheiros River

The connection to the landscape remains a highlight. The TV host calls the property a “floating house” because of the sense of freedom that the view of the Pinheiros River brings from high up in the building.

Virtual Tour on PodEntrar

In 2023, Luciana showcased details of the property on PodEntrar, hosted by Lucas Rangel. The tour revealed the pastel kitchen, the shoe closet, and a wall where she keeps old cell phones used throughout her life.

With information from TudoGostoso, Folha de S.Paulo.
